subject: maths
question: A rabbit and a fox are 1000 meters apart. If they sprint in the same direction, the fox overtakes the rabbit in 10 minutes. If they sprint toward one another, they pass each other in 2 minutes. What is the velocity of the rabbit in meters per minute?
solution:
**Given:**

Distance (D) = 1000 meters

Time (Same direction) = 10 minutes

Time (Opposite direction) = 2 minutes

Let velocity of fox = vf

Let velocity of rabbit = vᵣ

**Formula used:**

Relative speed (Same direction) = vf - vᵣ

Relative speed (Opposite direction) = vf + vᵣ

Speed = Distance / Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ vf - vᵣ = 1000 / 10

⇒ vf - vᵣ = 1000 / 10 = 100 (Equation 1)

⇒ vf + vᵣ = 1000 / 2

⇒ vf + vᵣ = 1000 / 2 = 500 (Equation 2)

Subtracting Equation 1 from Equation 2:

⇒ (vf + vᵣ) - (vf - vᵣ) = 500 - 100

⇒ 2vᵣ = 400

⇒ vᵣ = 400 / 2

⇒ vᵣ = 200

**∴ The velocity of the rabbit is 200 meters per minute.**
